title: Round 20 Pacific Northwest state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Oregon, Washington, and Idaho. Every seeded row reproduces one accepted USGS GNIS Geocoder candidate screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Political divisions, counties, census places, canals, ranges, reservations, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors/coastlines; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

knownLimitations: Oregon, Washington, and Idaho are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.
The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence, and the returned county is primary-county provenance.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain, coastlines, or corridors. All three frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Oregon/Washington rectangles include border and offshore context; the Idaho rectangle spans the panhandle outline and includes small areas outside Idaho. No boundary geometry is claimed.
